page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page of the opening) with one main text column; right-hand edge shows a narrow column of text from the facing page (partly cut off, fragments only); marginal notes at the right edge of the main column are cut into the text by the binding; running head at top.

main_text.l: 2. 1.Cor.11.v.26.27. quotiescunque
calicem bibetis: biberit calicem. 3. judicium
manducari & bibi. 1.Cor.11.v.29.
Hęc & similes locutiones aliæ figuratæ
omnes sunt & tropicæ: sed in ipsa institutione
Evangelistarum & Apostoli Pauli
invenitur, ut latius id ipsum declaravit Petr. Martyr
in Epist. de Eucharistia in Gardinerum in
loc. com. class. 4. cap. 10. Falsum ergo institutione[?]
verbis propriis constare. Poteft ex
his omnibus satis intelligi, quid vel novum
vel non novum in Eucharistiæ institutione,
& an novitas ea sit argumentum
proprietatis verborum.
17 V. Iterum urget verba in sede doctrinæ
ipsius necessario esse propria, ut verus & ipsius
haberi possit. Sed nos contrarium
probavimus ex articulo de sessione Christi ad
dextram Patris. Allegat vero Hieronymum
dixisse, ex solis figuris & allegoriis non posse
confirmari & comprobari dogmata: Et Augustinum
necesse esse, ut quicquid ex verbis
improprie, aut oratione figurata, ex sermone obscuro
& ambiguo per interpretationem eruitur, illud ut
πίστις fidei habeat certum & solidum
fundamentum, alibi in scripturis, propriis,
usitatis, & apertis verbis tradi & fundari. Ubi
hæc docuerint Hieronymus & Augustinus non no-
tavit, quod necessarium erat, ut e collatione

page.notes: Right-hand page largely cut off; only fragments of letters (tio, qu, fol, de, do, de, go, nil, ris, gu, nil, gia, va, cis, tu, bo, m, g, S, I, r, c, m, e, T, li, q) are visible at the binding edge and are not transcribed. Marginal notes at the inner edge of the left page are mostly illegible through the binding and staining; the marginal fragments "Cor. 11", "Ioan." and "Trident." are not legible enough to copy. Several words in the text are doubtful, notably the line "Falsum ergo institutione" and the Greek word in the final paragraph, which is marked uncertain.
